title: Local Noetherianity descends along an fppf scheme morphism
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Suppose that $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and surjective on underlying topological spaces [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. If $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], then $Y$ is locally Noetherian. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, reducedness, or Noetherian hypothesis on a common base scheme is imposed.

source.place: Tag 034C (lemma-Noetherian-local-fppf), descent implication for the singleton fppf covering; definition-property-local gives the meaning of locality.

proof.text: The singleton $\{f:X\to Y\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site], since its three defining conditions are precisely the hypotheses on $f$. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] it is an fpqc covering. Fix an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$. The finite-affine-open condition of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] supplies finitely many affine opens $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j\subseteq X$ with $\bigcup_j f(U_j)=V$. In particular every $f(U_j)$ lies in $V$. Empty $V$ may be handled by the empty family.

source.place: Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc), and definition-fpqc-covering; affine reduction used in descent.tex Tag 034C

proof.text: For every chosen affine open $U_j$ of $X$, its ring $B_j$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], because $X$ is locally Noetherian. Let $\varphi_j:A\to B_j$ be the ring map inducing the restricted morphism $U_j\to V$, using the affine spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The flatness of the original $f$, applied to the affine pair $(U_j,V)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], says that each $B_j$ is a flat $A$-module. No affineness of $f^{-1}(V)$ is required.

source.place: Tag 034C (lemma-Noetherian-local-fppf), affine descent reduction; properties.tex lemma-locally-Noetherian and morphisms.tex Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize)

proof.text: Put $B=\prod_j B_j$ with $A\to B$ given by $(\varphi_j)_j$. The finite product is flat over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules]. Its spectrum maps surjectively to $\operatorname{Spec}A$: given a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the covering in Step 1 gives an index $j$ and $\mathfrak q_j\in\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ with $\varphi_j^{-1}(\mathfrak q_j)=\mathfrak p$. The inverse image of $\mathfrak q_j$ along $B\to B_j$ is a prime of $B$, whose contraction to $A$ is $\mathfrak p$, by composition of inverse images. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] makes $A\to B$ faithfully flat.

source.place: Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings), applied to the finite product of affine-cover rings in the descent reduction of Tag 034C

proof.text: The finite product $B$ is Noetherian by the following elementary ideal argument. For an ideal $I\subseteq B$, let $I_j$ be its projection to $B_j$. Each $I_j$ is an ideal and has finitely many generators, because $B_j$ is Noetherian. Lift these generators to $I$ and multiply each lift by the coordinate idempotent $e_j\in B$, equal to $1$ in coordinate $j$ and $0$ elsewhere. The resulting finite collection generates $I$: every $b\in I$ is $\sum_j e_jb$, and its $j$-th coordinate is a $B_j$-linear combination of the chosen generators of $I_j$. For the empty product $B$ is the zero ring and its only ideal is generated by the empty set. This proves the finite-generation criterion in [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Noetherian rings, finite-generation-of-ideals definition; elementary finite-product argument in the affine reduction of descent.tex Tag 034C

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-descent-noetherian] to the faithfully flat map $A\to B$ of Step 3 and the Noetherian ring $B$ of Step 4. It follows that $A$ is Noetherian. The ring descent theorem imposes no finite-presentation or Noetherian assumption on $A$.

source.place: Tag 033E (lemma-descent-Noetherian), exactly as invoked in descent.tex Tag 034C

proof.text: Since $V$ was arbitrary, every affine open of $Y$ has Noetherian ring of sections. Choose an affine open cover of the scheme $Y$; it is a cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, so [pqf-def-locnoeth] gives that $Y$ is locally Noetherian. If $Y$ is empty the empty affine cover gives the same conclusion. The argument selected finitely many source opens separately over each affine $V$ and never required a finite cover of all of $Y$ or quasi-compactness of $f$.
